reasoning: Re-cut the deep rung under the August base. The deepest souvenir on the book. $448 described the 31 July gap-day close when MSFT was $464; at $513.53 it locks only +6.6% on a position at +22%. $476 sits below the 18 August low of 477.15 and beneath every close of the mid-August shelf, so it fires only if the 390-to-513 leg fails back through a month of structure, and locks +13.3% on 1 of 2. Deutsche Boerse is the second-cleanest structure on the STOXX 600 and the only one besides TKA where volume expands INTO the high rather than drying up at it. The 08/17 bar broke 270.80-275.00 congestion and closed 277.70 on 1.01x, and since then the low has been higher every single session: 270.80, 277.60, 274.20, 276.90, 278.80, 283.70, 282.10, 285.00, 286.20 — nine rungs, no give-back. The last two sessions printed 371,046 then 394,810 shares against a 311,187 60-day average (1.19x and 1.27x, rising two days running) and made outright 52-week highs at 289.30 then 290.30. RS +13.0pp over 3m and +25.5pp over 6m against VGK, positive on BOTH windows, which is my bar. This is the quiet, persistent EU move my mandate is built for. It does not get a market order: the tape is one session stale, so a >= level is the only honest instrument — 290.80 clears the 290.30 52-week intraday high by 0.2% and sits 0.69% over the 288.80 close, well inside my 2% staleness rule, so it fires on a genuine breakout close that only new data can produce, or never. 8 shares at 290.80 is 2,326 EUR, 23.6% of my 9,865 NAV, inside my 25% cap even on a 305 gap-through. Quoted in EUR, no FX leg.

Paired stop, same session as the entry — the stop ships with the entry, every time, and TKA already billed me once for writing one after the fact. 280.00 sits under the 282.10 low of 08/25, the lowest low of the last four sessions, and under the 280.70 top of the 08/18-08/21 congestion the stock broke out of, so it only fires if DB1 falls all the way back INTO the pre-breakout range. DB1's recent daily range is roughly 4 points, so 280.00 is about two and a half full ranges under the last low — a failure stop, not a noise stop, which is what a slow, orderly ladder like this one needs. From a 290.80 fill that is -3.7%, comfortably inside my -10% mandate. Sized 8 to match the entry exactly. Mutually exclusive with the entry on any close, so if the buy-stop never fires this rejects harmlessly into my inbox for one line of ledger.

Cutting a one-day-old thesis that failed its own test. Take the -$133 now rather than the -$151 the trigger would take a session later.

The other side of Friday's rotation, taken in the leader that is less stretched. Enterprise software gapped away from the tape on the same two sessions that broke my hard-money book: CRM 205.62 to 252.05 on 55.5M shares (4.6x base) with a follow-through to a new high, NOW 125.80 to 138.43 to 144.71 on 27.8M then 29.0M against a ~13M base, closing in the top 87% of its range both days. Initial stop placed the same session as the entry — I do not carry an unprotected line overnight in this book, and Friday is exactly why. 136.50 sits under the 8/28 low of 137.80, so the follow-through day itself has to fail before I am out, and above the 8/27 gap-day open of 130.48, so a normal retest of the gap leaves me in. 8.21 points below the 144.71 reference close is 1.04 times the 8/28 range of 7.92 — one clean daily range, the same standard I apply to every other line. Risk of roughly $131, 1.1% of NAV, against a two-day move on 2x volume.

~€327 shakeout bid at €9.35, just beneath the 08-23 low of €9.4979 and the entire six-session 9.50-10.76 consolidation floor — a flush level, not a chase and not under the move (the 08-19 breakout base at €8.19 is too far to be a retest). LINK is the strongest 20-day mover in the book (+37.4%) and at 96.1% of its 180-day high; the freed XRP capital goes to the leader making highs, not the leader making lower highs. Would take LINK to 130 units, ~11% of book, inside the 30% cap. Close the full silver line at market on redundancy rather than on the rail, and I want to be honest that this is a concentration decision, not a falsification one — silver at 67.00 is still above its 08-19 level of 65.73 and the metal has not broken structure, it has been sold to the bottom of a 67-69.5 range. What has broken is my own construction: gold -2.9%, silver -3.5% and Bitcoin -3.0% on the same session, with SPY at -0.2%, is the proof that 4GLD, PHAG and BTC are one trade at 40% of capital and that my three separate rails are one rail that fires three times. Of the three legs this is the one to give up: it is the highest-beta expression of a view I already hold in the lower-volatility instrument, and it is the only one that has never worked — 63.15 entry, then 62.83, 62.33, 61.80, 62.48, four closes and not one above cost, with Friday's SLV print of -4.4% putting Monday near 60.30 for roughly -4.5%. The 58.40 rail is doing nothing useful from there: it would pay -7.5% to tell me what the -4.5% already says about a position whose only argument is a thesis I keep in two other tickers. It also fixes the currency arithmetic I flagged and then only half-corrected: sterling was 21% across silver and Anglo American, two unrelated assets and one currency, and this takes GBP to 11% with Anglo standing alone as the sole London line.

Valero at 352.36 is a fresh 60-day high and the cleanest available expression of the divergence Friday actually paid: crude has round-tripped from 87.83 on 08-21 to 83.40, and the barrel and the margin have separated. XOM sits -5.5% off its high at 156.71, CVX 201.86, TTE.PA 74.17, BP.L 5.15, REP.MC 26.37 and OMV.VI 67.20 are all lower over twelve sessions in three currencies, while VLO 352.36, MPC 368.83 and PSX 244.01 closed at fresh 60-day highs on the same days. Producers need the price to rise; refiners need the spread to widen, and a falling input against firm product is precisely how it widens. That is the same one-fact-two-sides swap that took me out of Shell and into Kuehne+Nagel, and I am buying the purest of the three — Valero is refining with the least midstream and chemical ballast, and my style is the cleanest expression of a theme, not the most diversified version of it. The shape passes my own test: 340.41, 348.03, 346.59, 352.36 off a base at 340, a 1.50% average daily move with a worst day of -1.62% in twelve sessions, a staircase rather than the +5.5% single-day sympathy print that disqualified SAP from this slot. Four shares, 1,409 USD or about 1,209 EUR, 11.3% of a 10,660 book, well inside my 20% cap; seventh of twelve, and it clears on existing cash without needing the silver proceeds to settle. FX stance: this is the view as much as the asset. Taking USD from 10% to 21% is a deliberate dollar add on the premise that Friday's hard-asset unwind was a real-rates move rather than a fear move — the same force that sold gold supports the dollar, so an asset that gains from cheaper crude and a currency that gains from firmer real rates are the same trade twice, compounding rather than cancelling. If I am wrong and the euro extends past 1.1688, the currency leg costs me roughly what one bad session in the asset costs, which is a price I will pay to stop being a metals fund with an equity hobby.

Protective rail on the new Valero line at 336.40, shipped in the same session as the entry and sized to exactly what I hold — the two failures I have paid for this month were a missing trigger field and a mis-sized stop, and both are checked here. The level sits beneath the 340.41, 341.51 and 341.67 closes that form the shelf under this leg, above the 330.21 close of 08-12 that preceded the breakout, and is not resting on a visited close; the only trade through it was the 335.00 intraday low of 08-26, and equity triggers evaluate on the daily close, so an ordinary shakeout of that shape does not trip it. At -4.53% from 352.36 it is wider in percent than the -3.4% I gave Deutsche Boerse and level with the -4.1% on Kuehne+Nagel, and the comparison that matters is in daily ranges rather than percent: VLO moves 1.50% a day with a worst day of -1.62% in twelve sessions, so this is 3.0 ranges, the width I have settled on. It marks where the refining-margin leg is dead, not where I get nervous, and sits comfortably inside my -15% mandate stop. FX stance: written in dollars, so a firming euro stops me in USD and compounds the loss in EUR rather than cushioning it — the same asymmetry that ended Abbott, and precisely why the rail goes on at entry rather than after the first bad day when a currency leg is working against the asset leg.
